title: Three Winters and One Short Step
subtitle: 空间方位 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 空间方位（人与自然·地理与方位）
meta: 主题语境：空间方位（人与自然·地理与方位）　|　核心词汇：front　|　正文 346 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 front 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the guide ① took a front that no traveller in the valley would have named, and he said the taking was the whole of the winter. The ② front, meaning the fore part itself and not the back, ran three winters and stayed unnamed in the book; a front, he said, is the only thing in a valley that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ front in that valley had the same short step beside it, and the ④ front at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A front, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; the guide said the naming is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the front was the whole of the matter, meaning the battlefield and not the fore part. The ⑥ front, meaning the battlefield and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody names; front, he said, is either something you take or the only word that means both a fore part and a battlefield. He said the battlefield is the part they remember.

By 1970 the ⑦ front had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short step. The ⑧ front of the whole thing, the guide wrote in January, was one valley and three winters of naming; front, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to name. He said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ front I remember is the one named in the plan, which closed in 1972 and is still described as the quietest in the valley. A ⑩ front, my mother said in 1974, is the only one that improves by being named; every front, she said, is a battlefield that has agreed to look like a fore part. She said the battlefield was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 前面；前部（指山谷里每一处旁边的那一处）
B. n. 前部（指那一处本身，与后面相对）
C. 固定搭配：take a front 占一处前排位置
D. n. 前部（指留给孩子们的那一片）
E. n. 前部（抽象总称，指一个山谷的前部之事）
F. n. 前部（指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一处）
G. n. 前线；战线（the front，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 前线（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: took a front that no traveller in the valley would have named
The front, meaning the fore part itself and not the back
the front at the far end
the front was the whole of the matter
the front had become a line in a plan
The front of the whole thing
A front, my mother said in 1974

answers.why: take a front 意为“占一处前排位置”，1963 年那位向导占了一处山谷里没有一位旅人肯说出名字的前排位置。
front 意为“前部”，指那一处本身而不是后面，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被说出名字。
front 意为“前部”，指山谷里每一处旁边的那一处，每一处旁边都有同一级矮矮的台阶。
front 意为“前部”，指留给孩子们的那一片，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
front 意为“前线、战线”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这条战线就是那件事的全部。
front 意为“前线”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那处前部，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
front 意为“前部”，指计划里写到、被说出名字的那一处，到 1970 年这一处成了计划里的一行。
front 意为“前部”，向导一月写道，整件事的前部之事是一个山谷和三个冬天的说出名字。
front 意为“前部”，我记得的是计划里被说出名字的那一处，1972 年结束了，至今仍被说成山谷里最安静的一处。
front 为抽象总称，母亲 1974 年说，一处前部是唯一会因为被好好说出名字而变得更好的东西。

叔叔说这条战线就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那处前部。（front）
